dedupe_keys.name: coordination mechanisms for large scale reinforcement learning based adaptive traffic signal control

description: The implemented research develops coordination methods for adaptive traffic signals when individual reinforcement-learning agents observe only part of a large network. Neighbour communication and consensus-based learning address nonstationarity, while a decentralized partitioning method divides large transport networks into regions. The thesis describes a controller-design/evaluation methodology and algorithms intended to scale to hundreds of intersections. The description does not establish a tested maximum network size or provide a separately verified software release. Convergence statements are source claims, and operational traffic-light deployment is not inferred. Coverage is limited to the source-described systems and experiments. The related Zenodo deposit provides descriptive metadata, with restricted document or data access and licence label not stated. Document rights do not establish software rights or access to the underlying observations. Only full descriptive metadata, file inventories and the project metadata catalogue were reviewed; no underlying measurements, code, paper or model archive was opened. Its simulation role is agent-based coordination and optimization of traffic signals.
